pr_title: sql/schemachanger/*: optimize performance, primarily by adding support for containment
pr_body:
#### screl,scplan/rule: adopt containment

#### sql/schemachanger/rel: support inverted indexes and slice containment

This commit introduces some new concepts to rel:
* Slice attributes
* Inverted indexing of slice attributes
* Containment queries over slice attributes

One note is that the only support for containment queries is via an inverted
index. In the future, we could add direct containment evaluation such that if
we have a slice we could go iterate its members.

The basic idea is to introduce a slice membership type for the slice column
and to use the attribute in question to refer to the slice member value.

#### sql/schemachanger/rel: fix embedding support

#### sql/schemachanger/rel: optimize error checking
This change ends up making a huge difference. Otherwise, each subquery
invocation would lead to allocations which showed up in the profiles.

Fixes #86042

Release note: None

issue_context.title: drop database with hundreds of tables takes hours
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

The build for [django-cockroachdb](https://github.com/cockroachdb/django-cockroachdb) typically takes about an hour. A change in CockroachDB nightly between July 22 and August 3 increased the build time to around 24 hours. The tests run in the same amount of time, but the two `DROP DATABASE` queries at the conclusion of the test suite now take hours.

**Additional data / screenshots**

The roachtest build of django-cockroachdb which runs [some cluster queries](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/25fe0db12911a60571c3788b9403a6f42b52e003/pkg/cmd/roachtest/tests/orm_helpers.go#L38-L50) isn't affected by this performance regression.

**Environment:**
 - CockroachDB version: v22.2.0-alpha.00000000-2394-g6c24f3564e @ 2022/08/10 06:04:30


Jira issue: CRDB-18542

review_comments: I agree that maps are not worth mentioning, I find it very unlikely that we'll ever want them.

Just curious but how did this come about?
what about the other index we expanded with attributes `Attrs: []Attr{idx.Attrs[0], sliceSource, sliceIndex}` ?

This means that `EqualElements` does not mean what one might assume. I think we've reached the point where we need to surface the notion of keying an entity in the screl model. It is, after all, a relational model. Until now the key was assumed to be the tuple formed by all attributes. This change makes it become all attributes minus the slice attributes. It works, but I find it somewhat unsatisfying. Exposing this notion of key would have the added benefit of making the string representation of elements more compact and also stable. I've found its instability in the face of changes to the attributes in the model to be quite annoying, in the past.

At the very least we should rename `EqualElements` to `EqualKeys` and `equalityAttrs` to `keyEqualityAttrs`.
Do we support Maps and Arrays already?
